```python
"""Multi-provider frontier-model fallback chain for disclosure-rag enrichment.

Python counterpart to `apps/app/src/lib/ai/model-fallback.ts`. Same policy:
only current frontier models, never legacy tiers. Tiers are tried in order, a
tier is skipped when its credential is absent, and the chain moves on when a
tier errors — so one provider being down never takes enrichment down.

Two things this adds over the TS version, because this side runs *batches*
(104 podcast episodes x several prompts each) rather than one interactive
stream:

1. **Error classification.** A 401/403/404 is permanent — the tier is marked
   dead for the life of the process and skipped thereafter, so a revoked key
   costs one wasted round-trip per run instead of one per call. A 429/5xx/
   timeout is transient and gets a bounded retry with backoff.
2. **Attribution.** `complete()` returns which tier served the request, so
   callers can record truthfully whether enrichment actually happened. Silent
   degradation is how a whole ingestion run once recorded `status: ingested`
   on documents whose enrichment had 401'd.

Credential liveness verified 2026-08-07 against each provider's models
endpoint (see CHAIN comments). Dead-keyed tiers are deliberately retained:
they cost one attempt per process and light up automatically once the
credential is fixed, which is the graceful part.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
import random
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Status codes that mean "this tier will never work in this process".
PERMANENT_STATUS = {400, 401, 403, 404}
# Status codes worth retrying on the same tier before moving on.
TRANSIENT_STATUS = {408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504}

DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE = 0.1
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 1200


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tier:
    """One attempt in the fallback chain.

    `kind` selects the wire protocol, not the vendor: "anthropic" uses the
    Anthropic Messages API, "openai_compat" uses OpenAI's chat/completions
    shape, which DeepSeek, Together, Groq, and z.ai all serve. That keeps the
    dependency surface at two SDKs (both already installed) instead of one per
    provider.
    """

    id: str
    provider: str
    env_keys: Sequence[str]
    model: str
    kind: str = "openai_compat"
    base_url: Optional[str] = None
    max_retries: int = 0

    def api_key(self) -> Optional[str]:
        for key in self.env_keys:
            value = os.environ.get(key)
            if value:
                return value
        return None


# Ordering rationale: cheapest-capable frontier model first, then genuine
# vendor diversity. Tiers 1 and 2 share the Anthropic credential, so tier 3
# onward exists specifically to survive that key being revoked.
FRONTIER_FALLBACK_CHAIN: List[Tier] = [
    Tier(
        # Live 2026-08-07. Fast frontier — the right default for bulk
        # structured extraction over long transcripts.
        id="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5",
        provider="Claude Sonnet 5",
        env_keys=("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",),
        model="claude-sonnet-5",
        kind="anthropic",
    ),
    Tier(
        # Same credential as above — guards model-level failures, not key
        # revocation. Heavier, so it sits behind the fast tier.
        id="anthropic/claude-opus-4-8",
        provider="Claude Opus 4.8",
        env_keys=("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",),
        model="claude-opus-4-8",
        kind="anthropic",
    ),
    Tier(
        # Live 2026-08-07. First tier on a different vendor + credential.
        id="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro",
        provider="DeepSeek V4 Pro",
        env_keys=("DEEPSEEK_API_KEY",),
        model="deepseek-v4-pro",
        base_url="https://api.deepseek.com",
        max_retries=1,
    ),
    Tier(
        # Live 2026-08-07. Third distinct vendor.
        id="together/kimi-k3",
        provider="Kimi K3 (Together)",
        env_keys=("TOGETHERAI_API_KEY", "TOGETHER_API_KEY"),
        model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
        base_url="https://api.together.xyz/v1",
        max_retries=1,
    ),
    Tier(
        # Key returned 401 on 2026-08-07 (a valid key exists at the repo root).
        # Retained: costs one attempt per process, activates when fixed.
        id="openai/gpt-5.5",
        provider="GPT-5.5",
        env_keys=("OPENAI_API_KEY",),
        model="gpt-5.5",
        base_url=None,
    ),
    Tier(
        # Key returned 401 on 2026-08-07. Same rationale as above.
        id="groq/gpt-oss-120b",
        provider="GPT-OSS 120B (Groq)",
        env_keys=("GROQ_API_KEY",),
        model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
    ),
    Tier(
        # No ZHIPU_API_KEY/GLM_API_KEY in this app's env — skipped for free,
        # present so parity with the TS chain is explicit rather than an
        # oversight.
        id="zhipu/glm-5.2",
        provider="GLM-5.2",
        env_keys=("ZHIPU_API_KEY", "GLM_API_KEY"),
        model="glm-5.2",
        base_url="https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4",
    ),
]


@dataclass
class LLMResult:
    """A completion plus the provenance needed to record it honestly."""

    text: str
    tier_id: str
    provider: str
    attempts: int
    degraded: bool  # served by something other than the first enabled tier


class AllProvidersFailed(RuntimeError):
    """Every enabled tier failed. Carries the per-tier reasons."""

    def __init__(self, failures: Dict[str, str]):
        self.failures = failures
        detail = "; ".join(f"{tier}: {err}" for tier, err in failures.items()) or "no tiers enabled"
        super().__init__(f"All LLM providers failed ({detail})")


def _status_of(exc: Exception) -> Optional[int]:
    """Best-effort HTTP status from an SDK exception.

    Both the openai and anthropic SDKs raise APIStatusError subclasses
    carrying `.status_code`; httpx errors carry `.response.status_code`.
    """
    status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
    if isinstance(status, int):
        return status
    response = getattr(exc, "response", None)
    status = getattr(response, "status_code", None)
    return status if isinstance(status, int) else None


def _is_permanent(exc: Exception) -> bool:
    status = _status_of(exc)
    if status is not None:
        return status in PERMANENT_STATUS
    # No status: an import failure or client-construction error is permanent;
    # a network blip is not.
    return isinstance(exc, (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError))


def _is_transient(exc: Exception) -> bool:
    status = _status_of(exc)
    if status is not None:
        return status in TRANSIENT_STATUS
    return not isinstance(exc, (ImportError, ModuleNotFoundError))


class LLMFallback:
    """Ordered frontier chain with per-tier retry and dead-tier caching."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        tiers: Optional[Sequence[Tier]] = None,
        *,
        prefer_provider: Optional[str] = None,
        backoff_base: float = 0.75,
    ):
        chain = list(tiers if tiers is not None else FRONTIER_FALLBACK_CHAIN)
        prefer = (prefer_provider or os.getenv("RAG_PIPELINE_PROVIDER") or "").lower().strip()
        if prefer:
            # Stable partition: preferred vendor's tiers first, order preserved.
            chain.sort(key=lambda t: 0 if prefer in t.id.lower() else 1)
        self.tiers = chain
        self.backoff_base = backoff_base
        self._dead: Dict[str, str] = {}
        self._clients: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    # -- introspection ----------------------------------------------------

    def enabled_tiers(self) -> List[Tier]:
        """Tiers with a credential present and not yet proven dead."""
        return [t for t in self.tiers if t.api_key() and t.id not in self._dead]

    def describe(self) -> str:
        enabled = self.enabled_tiers()
        if not enabled:
            return "no enabled tiers"
        return " -> ".join(t.id for t in enabled)

    # -- clients ----------------------------------------------------------

    def _client(self, tier: Tier):
        if tier.id in self._clients:
            return self._clients[tier.id]
        key = tier.api_key()
        if tier.kind == "anthropic":
            from anthropic import Anthropic

            client = Anthropic(api_key=key)
        else:
            from openai import OpenAI

            client = OpenAI(api_key=key, base_url=tier.base_url) if tier.base_url else OpenAI(api_key=key)
        self._clients[tier.id] = client
        return client

    def _invoke(
        self,
        tier: Tier,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_content: str,
        temperature: float,
        max_tokens: int,
    ) -> str:
        client = self._client(tier)
        if tier.kind == "anthropic":
            message = client.messages.create(
                model=tier.model,
                max_tokens=max_tokens,
                temperature=temperature,
                system=system_prompt,
                messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
            )
            return "".join(block.text for block in message.content if getattr(block, "type", "") == "text")
        response = client.chat.completions.create(
            model=tier.model,
            temperature=temperature,
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            messages=[
                {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
                {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
            ],
        )
        return response.choices[0].message.content or ""

    # -- public API -------------------------------------------------------

    def complete(
        self,
        system_prompt: str,
        user_content: str,
        *,
        temperature: float = DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE,
        max_tokens: int = DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS,
    ) -> LLMResult:
        """Run the chain, returning the first success and its provenance.

        Raises AllProvidersFailed only when every enabled tier is exhausted.
        """
        failures: Dict[str, str] = {}
        attempts = 0
        first_enabled = None

        for tier in self.tiers:
            if not tier.api_key():
                continue  # credential absent — free skip, not a failure
            if first_enabled is None:
                first_enabled = tier.id
            if tier.id in self._dead:
                failures.setdefault(tier.id, f"skipped ({self._dead[tier.id]})")
                continue

            for attempt in range(1, tier.max_retries + 2):
                attempts += 1
                try:
                    text = self._invoke(tier, system_prompt, user_content, temperature, max_tokens)
                    if not text.strip():
                        raise RuntimeError("provider returned empty text")
                    if tier.id != first_enabled:
                        logger.info("LLM fallback: served by %s (degraded from %s)", tier.id, first_enabled)
                    return LLMResult(
                        text=text,
                        tier_id=tier.id,
                        provider=tier.provider,
                        attempts=attempts,
                        degraded=tier.id != first_enabled,
                    )
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - classified below
                    reason = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
                    failures[tier.id] = reason
                    if _is_permanent(exc):
                        status = _status_of(exc)
                        self._dead[tier.id] = f"HTTP {status}" if status else type(exc).__name__
                        logger.warning(
                            "LLM tier %s permanently unavailable (%s) — skipping for the rest of this run",
                            tier.id, self._dead[tier.id],
                        )
                        break
                    last_attempt = attempt >= tier.max_retries + 1
                    if last_attempt or not _is_transient(exc):
                        logger.warning("LLM tier %s failed (%s) — trying next tier", tier.id, reason)
                        break
                    delay = self.backoff_base * (2 ** (attempt - 1)) * (1 + random.random() * 0.25)
                    logger.warning(
                        "LLM tier %s attempt %d failed (%s) — retrying in %.1fs",
                        tier.id, attempt, reason, delay,
                    )
                    time.sleep(delay)

        raise AllProvidersFailed(failures)


_SHARED: Optional[LLMFallback] = None


def get_fallback(prefer_provider: Optional[str] = None) -> LLMFallback:
    """Process-wide chain, so the dead-tier cache is shared across callers."""
    global _SHARED
    if _SHARED is None:
        _SHARED = LLMFallback(prefer_provider=prefer_provider)
    return _SHARED
```

Enrichment (classification, NER, embeddable texts) cannot run in `apps/disclosure-rag` because no configured frontier credential is usable. Verified 2026-08-07 by probing each provider's models endpoint plus a live completion.

| Key (in `apps/disclosure-rag/.env`) | models endpoint | actual completion |
|---|---|---|
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | 401 | 401 invalid_api_key |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **200** | **400 "credit balance is too low"** |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` | 401 | 401 |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | 400 "API key not valid" | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | 403 **"reported as leaked"** | — |
| `XAI_API_KEY` | 403 | — |
| `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | 401 | — |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | 200 | **works** |
| `TOGETHERAI_API_KEY` | 200 | **works** |

Two traps worth recording:

1. **A models-list 200 does not prove usability.** Anthropic lists `claude-opus-5`/`claude-sonnet-5` fine and then 400s on every completion for lack of credit.
2. A **valid** `OPENAI_API_KEY` exists in the **repo root `.env`** (different key, returns 200). The disclosure-rag copy is stale. Deliberately not copied — that is a credential decision for the owner. An alternative worth considering is adding the repo-root `.env` as a fallback layer in this app's dotenv chain, but that silently changes which key wins for everything else in the app, so it needs a deliberate call.

**Impact:** with only DeepSeek + Together live, the fallback chain (see related ticket) still works, but the two Anthropic tiers burn one wasted call each per process before being cached as dead.

**Done when:** `apps/disclosure-rag/.env` has a working `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and either Anthropic billing is topped up or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is removed so its tiers skip for free.

`lib/llm_fallback.py` (added 2026-08-07) gives disclosure-rag a frontier fallback chain with error classification, dead-tier caching, a reasoning-model token floor, and tier attribution. Only `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py` currently uses it.

At least 14 other call sites still hand-roll their own provider logic and will keep failing independently — during the first run after the port, `processing/content_analysis.py:59` still printed `Claude Analysis Error: 400 credit balance too low` from its own Anthropic client.

Sites found by `grep -rn "messages.create\|chat.completions.create" --include="*.py"`:

- `processing/content_analysis.py:59,77,104,138`
- `processing/enhanced_content_analysis.py:226,246,264`
- `agents/entity_extraction_agent.py:415,440`
- `lib/transcript_fidelity.py:148` (the optional `--llm-review` pass)
- `disclosure_chat.py:141,150`, `disclosure_chat_with_memory.py:196`
- `activate_agno.py:170,177,240,247,385,392`

Several of these also pin **legacy** model IDs, which violates the frontier-only policy the repo already encodes in `apps/app/src/lib/ai/model-fallback.ts`. `rag_prompt_pipeline.py` had `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` and `gpt-4o-mini` before the port.

**Done when:** each site either calls `get_fallback().complete(...)` or has a comment justifying why it needs a specific provider. No legacy model ID remains in `apps/disclosure-rag`.

Related: DMGD-152 (same gap on the Prometheus/TS side).

<tool-use data-tool-type="unknown" data-tool-name="mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **mcp__claude_ai_Linear__save_issue**</summary>
`review_transcript` scores a `coverage` subscore by comparing captured caption seconds against the episode's real duration. When the duration is unknown it substitutes a neutral prior of 0.75 (`transcript_fidelity.py`, `subs["coverage"] = 0.75  # unknown duration: mild neutral prior`).

`enumerate_playlist` uses `extract_flat: "in_playlist"`, which for this playlist returns `duration: None` on every entry. So `expected_seconds` is always null and coverage is never actually measured — an episode whose captions cover only the first 10 minutes of a 3-hour show would still score 0.75 on that dimension.

Observed on `K4gYHs84BIc`: `covered_seconds: 11933.0, expected_seconds: null, subscores.coverage: 0.75`.

Options:
1. Fetch per-video durations (accurate, but ~104 extra yt-dlp round-trips per run).
2. Derive expected duration from the last caption timestamp — nearly free, but can't detect captions truncated at the end, which is the failure mode coverage exists to catch.
3. Leave the prior and mark the coverage dimension explicitly unmeasured in the fidelity JSON so it isn't mistaken for a real signal.

**Done when:** either coverage is measured against a real duration, or the report distinguishes "measured" from "assumed" so the gate isn't trusted beyond what it checks.

```text
def process_url(url: str, upload: bool = False, add_to_kb: bool = True) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Process a URL (web page or YouTube video) with enhanced mem0 integration"""
    _import_heavy_dependencies()
    logger.info(f"Processing URL: {url}")
    stages: List[Dict[str, str]] = []
    youtube = is_youtube_url(url)
    content_type = "youtube_video" if youtube else "web_article"
    extraction_stage_name = (
        "YouTube transcript extraction" if youtube else "Web content extraction")

    # process_youtube_url_enhanced/process_web_url_enhanced were previously
    # called unguarded here, so any exception they raised (network error,
    # malformed response, etc.) propagated out of process_url entirely -
    # main.py's CLI would crash with a raw traceback instead of an honest
    # "❌ Processing failed" report, and playlist_ingestion.py (which calls
    # process_url directly for every playlist episode) would only learn
    # `str(e)` with no stage_report at all (T-045 M3).
    try:
        if youtube:
            result = process_youtube_url_enhanced(url, upload, add_to_kb)
        else:
            result = process_web_url_enhanced(url, upload, add_to_kb)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception(f"Error processing URL: {url}")
        stages.append(_stage(extraction_stage_name, False, str(e)))
        return {"source": url, "title": url, "stage_report": stages}

    stages.append(_stage(extraction_stage_name, result is not None))

    if result is None:
        return None

    # Add mem0 integration for web articles (YouTube already has it in generate_transcript)
    if not youtube:
        try:
            from lib.mem0_integration import add_web_article_memory
            stages.append(_call_mem0(
                "Mem0 web article memory", add_web_article_memory,
                title=result.get('title', 'Unknown'),
                url=url,
                content=result.get('content', ''),
                summary=result.get('analysis', ''),
                tags=result.get('tags', [])
            ))
        except ImportError as e:
            stages.append(_skipped("Mem0 web article memory", f"module unavailable: {e}"))

    # Add CocoIndex knowledge graph processing if result has doc_id.
    # process_web_with_enhanced_workflow() already runs CocoIndex internally
    # (knowledge_base_service.py:~735-785); triggering it again here for web
    # results ran a second, global `cocoindex update` on every web ingestion.
    # The YouTube workflow has no internal CocoIndex step, so it still needs
    # this pass.
    if result.get('doc_id') and add_to_kb and youtube:
        try:
            display.print_stage("🕸️ KNOWLEDGE GRAPH", "🕸️")
            display.start_spinner(
                "📊 Building knowledge graph with CocoIndex...")

            cocoindex_result = trigger_cocoindex_processing(result['doc_id'])
            if cocoindex_result and cocoindex_result.get('status') == 'success':
                entities_count = cocoindex_result.get('entities_processed', 0)
                relationships_count = cocoindex_result.get(
                    'relationships_processed', 0)
                display.stop_spinner(
                    f"✅ Knowledge graph built: {entities_count} entities, {relationships_count} relationships")
                result['cocoindex_processing'] = cocoindex_result
                stages.append(_stage(
                    "Knowledge graph construction", True,
                    f"{entities_count} entities, {relationships_count} relationships"))

                try:
                    from lib.mem0_integration import add_knowledge_graph_memory
                    stages.append(_call_mem0(
                        "Mem0 knowledge graph memory", add_knowledge_graph_memory,
                        doc_id=result['doc_id'],
                        entities_processed=entities_count,
                        relationships_processed=relationships_count,
                        kg_results=cocoindex_result
                    ))
                except ImportError as e:
                    stages.append(_skipped("Mem0 knowledge graph memory", f"module unavailable: {e}"))
            elif cocoindex_result and cocoindex_result.get('status') == 'skipped':
                display.stop_spinner(
                    f"⚠️ Knowledge graph processing skipped: {cocoindex_result.get('reason', 'unknown')}")
                result['cocoindex_processing'] = cocoindex_result
                stages.append(_skipped(
                    "Knowledge graph construction", cocoindex_result.get('reason', 'unknown')))
            else:
                display.stop_spinner("❌ Knowledge graph processing failed")
                if cocoindex_result:
                    result['cocoindex_processing'] = cocoindex_result
```

```md
---
name: provider-key-liveness-probing
description: "A models-list 200 does not mean an LLM key works — probe with a real completion; most provider keys in this repo are dead"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

Verified 2026-08-07 by probing every provider key in `apps/disclosure-rag/.env`:

| Key | `/models` | real completion |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **200** | **400 "credit balance is too low"** |
| `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | 200 | works (`deepseek-v4-pro`) |
| `TOGETHERAI_API_KEY` | 200 | works (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`) |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | 401 | 401 — **but the repo-root `.env` has a different, working key** |
| `GROQ_API_KEY` / `XAI_API_KEY` / `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | 401/403 | — |
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | 400 "not valid" | — |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` | 403 **"reported as leaked"** | — |

**The trap:** Anthropic's models endpoint returns 200 and happily lists
`claude-opus-5`/`claude-sonnet-5` on a key with no credit. A liveness table built
from `/models` alone says "Anthropic is live" and is wrong. Always probe with an
actual completion before believing a key works, and before designing a fallback
chain around it.

**Second trap:** `deepseek-v4-pro` and `Kimi-K3` are **reasoning models** — they
bill chain-of-thought against `max_tokens`. At `max_tokens=16` both return
`finish_reason="length"` with **empty** `content`; at 800 both answer correctly.
An empty response from these reads exactly like a broken provider. `lib/llm_fallback.py`
handles this with a `reasoning` flag and a 2048-token floor.

Related: [[frontier-models-only-policy]] (the chain must use frontier IDs only),
and the TS counterpart `apps/app/src/lib/ai/model-fallback.ts`, whose comment
already records the same Gemini-leaked-key finding.

```

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-5 2026-08-07 02:27:32Z)**_

The end-to-end run is still in flight (a 36k-word transcript takes several minutes through Upstash sync + embeddings); the background waiter will report when it lands. Here's where things stand.

## Graceful fallback provider set — built and working

New module: `apps/disclosure-rag/lib/llm_fallback.py` (402 lines), the Python counterpart to the TS `model-fallback.ts` chain. `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py` now uses it — its old two-provider block (81 lines) is gone.

**I did not blind-port the TS chain**, because probing showed most of its credentials are dead here. Verified by hitting each provider's models endpoint *and* a real completion:

| Provider | `/models` | real completion |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | 200 | **400 "credit balance is too low"** |
| DeepSeek | 200 | ✅ works |
| TogetherAI | 200 | ✅ works |
| OpenAI / Groq / xAI / AI Gateway | 401/403 | — |
| Google | 400 "not valid" · Gemini 403 **"reported as leaked"** | — |

That first row is the trap worth naming: **a models-list 200 does not mean the key works.** Anthropic cheerfully lists `claude-opus-5`/`claude-sonnet-5` on a key with zero credit. My initial liveness table said "Anthropic is live" and was wrong; only the completion probe caught it.

Four things the chain does beyond try-then-next:

- **Error classification.** 401/403/404 → tier marked dead for the process. A revoked key costs one round-trip *per run*, not per call. Measured: call 1 took 3 attempts, call 2 took 1.
- **400 is not blanket-permanent.** "credit balance"/"quota"/"billing" kills the tier; a malformed single request doesn't — otherwise one bad document would disable a working provider for the remaining 100 episodes.
- **Reasoning-model token floor.** DeepSeek V4 and Kimi K3 bill chain-of-thought against `max_tokens`: at 16 both return `finish_reason="length"` with *empty* content, at 800 both answer. That looks identical to a broken provider. Tiers carry a `reasoning` flag with a 2048 floor, and `BudgetExhausted` retries at double. **This fired twice in the real pipeline run and recovered** — it was a live hazard against the pipeline's 1200-token default, not a hypothetical.
- **Attribution.** `complete()` returns which tier served and whether it degraded.

Live chain: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 → claude-opus-4-8 → deepseek-v4-pro → kimi-k3 → gpt-5.5 → gpt-oss-120b`. Dead-keyed tiers are kept deliberately — they cost one attempt and light up when credentials are fixed.

## The silent-success bug, which was worse than it looked

Chasing why `rag_status` came back `None`, I traced the actual call graph: `process_url` → `process_youtube_with_enhanced_workflow` → `lib/youtube.py:227`, which files enrichment status under the transcript's *file* metadata — a different shape from `process_file`, which sets `result['rag_pipeline']`. My first fix read one shape and silently fell through to "ingested" on the other.

`_enrichment_outcome()` now probes all three known locations and returns **`unknown`** when it finds nothing, rather than assuming success. Unit-tested across five shapes:

```
process_file shape   -> ('error', '401 bad key')
metadata shape       -> ('ok', '')
stage_report ok      -> ('ok', 'embeddable=12')
stage_report fail    -> ('error', 'All LLM providers failed')
nothing reported     -> ('unknown', '')
```

Run reports gained an `Enrichment` column so a degraded run is visible without reading `state.json`.

## Tickets

Four filed before the Linear MCP server disconnected mid-session:

- **DMGD-212** (Urgent) — dead credentials, with the full probe table and the note that a working `OPENAI_API_KEY` sits in the repo root `.env`
- **DMGD-213** (High) — 14 remaining hand-rolled call sites, several pinning legacy model IDs; related to DMGD-152
- **DMGD-214** (High) — ingest remaining 101 episodes
- **DMGD-215** (Med) — fidelity coverage runs on a 0.75 prior

Six I could not file once the server dropped: spacetime sources `sightings` not `events` (decision ticket — that's your call, not mine to presume); fabricated `credibilityScore`/`epistemicStatus`; globe `pointer-events` 0/361; black-screen time-to-first-content; store-write-during-render at `spacetime-canvas.tsx:301`; `/run-skill-generator` for the Mapbox fiber-walk driver. Say the word and I'll file them when Linear reconnects.

## Honest status

Verified: module behavior in isolation, error classification, dead-tier caching, token floor, budget retry firing in the real pipeline, the grader's five shapes, and `py_compile` on all three files. **Not yet verified:** the final `rag_status` landing in `state.json` and the run report — that run is still executing. Per the repo's Definition of Done, that piece is **UNVERIFIED** until it completes.

Nothing committed — the tree has ~98 unrelated modified files, so staging is yours. Changed: `lib/llm_fallback.py` (new), `processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py`, `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`, `lib/transcript_fidelity.py`. Also recorded the key-probing lesson to memory.

```python
"""Verify enrichment status survives the YouTube path into process_url's result.

Stubs ONLY the network boundary (generate_transcript). Everything downstream —
the data-dict construction in knowledge_base_service and the grader in
playlist_ingestion — is the real code.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))

import lib.youtube as yt  # noqa: E402
from lib.knowledge_base_service import KnowledgeBaseService  # noqa: E402

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("scripts"))
from playlist_ingestion import _enrichment_outcome  # noqa: E402

tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()


def make_files(rag_block):
    tpath = os.path.join(tmp, "t.txt")
    mpath = os.path.join(tmp, "t_metadata.json")
    with open(tpath, "w") as f:
        f.write("transcript body")
    meta = {"title": "Ep", "id": "vid123", "categories": [], "tags": [],
            "description": "", "chapters": []}
    if rag_block is not None:
        meta["rag_pipeline"] = rag_block
    with open(mpath, "w") as f:
        json.dump(meta, f)
    return {"file_path": tpath, "metadata_path": mpath}


CASES = [
    ("enrichment failed (401)",
     {"status": "error", "embeddable_count": 0, "errors": ["All LLM providers failed: 401"]}),
    ("enrichment ok",
     {"status": "ok", "embeddable_count": 12, "errors": []}),
    ("no rag block at all", None),
]

svc = KnowledgeBaseService()
fails = []
for label, block in CASES:
    yt.generate_transcript = lambda url, _b=block: make_files(_b)
    import lib.knowledge_base_service as kbs
    kbs.KnowledgeBaseService.__module__  # keep import used
    result = svc.process_youtube_with_enhanced_workflow(
        "https://youtube.com/watch?v=vid123", upload=False, add_to_kb=False)
    if result is None:
        print(f"  {label}: workflow returned None")
        fails.append(label)
        continue
    top = result.get("rag_pipeline")
    nested = (result.get("metadata") or {}).get("rag_pipeline")
    status, detail = _enrichment_outcome(result)
    print(f"  {label}:")
    print(f"      top-level rag_pipeline present : {top is not None and top != {}}")
    print(f"      metadata.rag_pipeline present  : {nested is not None and nested != {}}")
    print(f"      _enrichment_outcome            : {status!r}  detail={detail[:60]!r}")
    expected = {"enrichment failed (401)": "error", "enrichment ok": "ok",
                "no rag block at all": "unknown"}[label]
    if status != expected:
        print(f"      MISMATCH expected {expected!r}")
        fails.append(label)

print()
print("RESULT:", "all cases correct" if not fails else f"FAILED: {fails}")
sys.exit(1 if fails else 0)

```

```text
    """Write metadata to a JSON file with updated path structure"""
    video_title = clean_string(title)
    file_name = f"{video_title}_metadata.json"
    folder_path = get_folder_path_from_metadata(metadata)

    if not os.path.exists(folder_path):
        os.makedirs(folder_path)

    file_path = os.path.join(folder_path, file_name)

    with open(file_path, "w", encoding='utf-8') as file:
        json.dump(metadata, file, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

    print(f"Metadata saved to {file_name}")
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-08-07 02:34:09Z)**_

I picked up where the agent died mid-diagnosis and closed the bug it was chasing.

**The bug it was on.** Its dying words were `rag=None — process_url doesn't return rag_pipeline at the top level`. That's right, but the cause is one layer deeper: `process_youtube_with_enhanced_workflow` builds its `data['metadata']` from a hand-written key whitelist (`video_id, channel, duration, upload_date, url, type, categories, tags, description, chapters`) that simply doesn't copy `rag_pipeline` through. The web path (`web_content_processor.py:600`) and the local-file path (`main.py:503`) both surface it; YouTube — the only path playlists use — dropped it. So all four probes in the agent's `_enrichment_outcome` missed and every episode graded `unknown`.

**Confirmed live, not just read.** The subagent's long-running end-to-end run landed at 02:31:21 on pre-fix code:

```
K4gYHs84BIc | status: ingested | rag_status: "unknown"
```

Before that, two episodes were recorded `ingested` with `rag_status` absent entirely — including one at `fidelity: 0.5`, the dead-gate fallback value.

**The fix** propagates enrichment status from `generate_transcript`'s return value (the full dict, with errors), falling back to the metadata-file summary; `lib/youtube.py` now carries `errors` in that summary so a 401 can say why. Verified through the real workflow and the real grader with only the network boundary stubbed:

```
401 via generate_transcript return  → 'error'    detail='All LLM providers failed: 401'
ok  via generate_transcript return  → 'ok'
401 via metadata file fallback      → 'error'
skipped status                      → 'skipped'  → records enrichment_failed
no rag block at all                 → 'unknown'
```

That last case is the pre-fix behavior for every episode.

**Resume semantics check out:** `DONE_STATUSES = {"ingested", "quarantined"}`, so `enrichment_failed` is retried without `--force`. Once a working key is in place, the failed episodes get re-ingested rather than sitting permanently skipped.

**Two more defects fixed while in there.** `record()` merged into the existing entry, so a failed retry inherited the prior attempt's fields — my `no_transcript` run left a stale `fidelity: 0.922` and `doc_id` behind, reading as though a fetch that never happened had produced a document. Per-attempt outcome keys are now cleared before each write. Also fixed the type error at line 205 (`.get()` with a possibly-`None` key).

**What is not verified.** I could not land a post-fix live end-to-end run — both attempts returned `no_transcript`, YouTube throttling transcript fetches after the session's earlier runs. The seam test exercises the real code on both sides of the boundary but stubs the fetch, so per the repo's Definition of Done the full path is **UNVERIFIED**. Retry when the throttle clears. Separately, `llm_fallback.py` (402 new lines) and the `rag_prompt_pipeline.py` rewrite are the subagent's work and unreviewed by me — I verified the enrichment-grading path, not the provider chain. Its `llm_fallback.py:285` Pyright error is a union-narrowing false positive; `_invoke` branches on `tier.kind` before touching `.messages`.

```text
4	import {sightingsToSpacetimeEvents} from '../lib/normalize'

7	
8	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsInput {
9	  startYear?: number
10	  endYear?: number
11	  limit?: number
12	}
13	
14	export interface LoadSpacetimeEventsResult {
15	  events: SpacetimeEvent[]
16	  stations: TemporalStation[]
17	  timeRange: {startYear: number; endYear: number}
18	  /** Events that have coordinates — what the globe can render */
19	  geolocatedCount: number
20	}
21	
22	const DECADE_SPAN = 10
23	
24	/**
25	 * M0.5 data path: bounded Postgres query → SpacetimeEvent[] + stations.
26	 *
27	 * Uses the existing `getSightingsByTimeChunk` service (same substrate as
28	 * `/api/disclosure/uap-sightings`) via a server action so the canvas does
29	 * not need the INTERNAL_API_KEY header the REST route requires.
30	 *
31	 * Wide ranges are sampled per decade so `ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT n`
32	 * cannot collapse the canvas into only the most recent years.
33	 *
34	 * Does NOT load static `/sightings.geojson`.
35	 */
36	export async function loadSpacetimeEvents(
37	  input: LoadSpacetimeEventsInput = {},
38	): Promise<LoadSpacetimeEventsResult> {
39	  const startYear = input.startYear ?? 1940
40	  const endYear = input.endYear ?? new Date().getUTCFullYear()
41	  // Keep first paint bounded; later milestones page by viewport + cursor.
42	  const limit = Math.min(input.limit ?? 400, 800)
43	
44	  const sightings = await fetchStratifiedSightings(startYear, endYear, limit)
45	  const events = sightingsToSpacetimeEvents(sightings).sort(
46	    (a, b) => new Date(a.timestamp).getTime() - new Date(b.timestamp).getTime(),
47	  )
48	  const stations = buildTemporalStations(events, {
49	    historicalStartYear: startYear,
50	    historicalEndYear: endYear,
51	  })
52	
53	  return {
54	    events,
55	    stations,
56	    timeRange: {startYear, endYear},
57	    geolocatedCount: events.filter((e) => e.coordinates).length,
58	  }
59	}
60	
61	async function fetchStratifiedSightings(
62	  startYear: number,
63	  endYear: number,
64	  limit: number,
65	) {
66	  const span = Math.max(1, endYear - startYear + 1)
67	
68	  // Narrow windows: one query is fine.
69	  if (span <= DECADE_SPAN) {
70	    return getSightingsByTimeChunk(startYear, endYear, limit)
71	  }
72	
73	  const decades: Array<{from: number; to: number}> = []
74	  const startDecade = Math.floor(startYear / DECADE_SPAN) * DECADE_SPAN
75	  for (let year = startDecade; year <= endYear; year += DECADE_SPAN) {
76	    const from = Math.max(startYear, year)
77	    const to = Math.min(endYear, year + DECADE_SPAN - 1)
78	    if (from <= to) decades.push({from, to})
79	  }
80	
81	  const perDecade = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(limit / decades.length))
82	  const batches = await Promise.all(
83	    decades.map(({from, to}) => getSightingsByTimeChunk(from, to, perDecade)),
84	  )
85	
86	  const byId = new Map<string, (typeof batches)[number][number]>()
87	  for (const batch of batches) {
88	    for (const sighting of batch) {
89	      byId.set(sighting.id, sighting)
90	    }
91	  }
92	
93	  return [...byId.values()]
94	    .sort((a, b) => a.timestamp.getTime() - b.timestamp.getTime())
95	    .slice(0, limit)
96	}
```

```text
27	}

29	/**
30	 * Get aggregate statistics for events based on time range
31	 */
32	export async function getEventsStats(
33	  startYear: number = 1940,
34	  endYear: number = new Date().getFullYear()
35	) {
36	  try {
37	    const start = `${startYear}-01-01T00:00:00Z`;
38	    const end = `${endYear}-12-31T23:59:59Z`;
39	    const sql = getSql();
40	
41	    // category is a text[] column — unnest to count per category value
42	    const categoryRows = await sql`
43	      SELECT cat AS category, count(*)::int AS count
44	      FROM events,
45	           LATERAL unnest(category) AS cat
46	      WHERE date >= ${start}::timestamptz AND date <= ${end}::timestamptz
47	        AND category IS NOT NULL
48	      GROUP BY cat
49	      ORDER BY count DESC
50	    ` as { category: string; count: number }[];
51	
52	    const timeSeriesRows = await aggregateEventsByYear(start, end);
53	
54	    const locationRows = await sql`
55	      SELECT location, count(*)::int AS count
56	      FROM events
57	      WHERE date >= ${start}::timestamptz AND date <= ${end}::timestamptz
58	        AND location IS NOT NULL
59	      GROUP BY location
60	      ORDER BY count DESC
61	    ` as { location: string; count: number }[];
62	
63	    return {
64	      total: timeSeriesRows.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.count, 0),
65	      categoryDistribution: categoryRows,
66	      timeseriesData: timeSeriesRows,
67	      locationData: locationRows,
68	      timeRange: {

70	        endYear
71	      }
72	    };
```

Simulate the exact stratified fetch against the real database

```bash
cd packages/db && node --input-type=module -e "
import {neon} from '@neondatabase/serverless'
import fs from 'node:fs'
const url = fs.readFileSync('.env','utf8').match(/^DATABASE_URL=[\"']?([^\"'\n]+)/m)[1]
const sql = neon(url)
const DECADE=10, MAX_WINDOWS=24, startYear=100, endYear=2026, limit=400
const span=Math.max(1,endYear-startYear+1)
const windowSize=Math.ceil(span/MAX_WINDOWS/DECADE)*DECADE || DECADE
const windows=[]
const first=Math.floor(startYear/windowSize)*windowSize
for(let y=first;y<=endYear;y+=windowSize){
  const from=Math.max(startYear,y), to=Math.min(endYear,y+windowSize-1)
  if(from<=to) windows.push({from,to})
}
const perWindow=Math.max(20,Math.ceil(limit/windows.length))
console.log('windowSize',windowSize,'windows',windows.length,'perWindow',perWindow)
const pad=y=>String(y).padStart(4,'0')
const batches=await Promise.all(windows.map(({from,to})=>
  sql.query('select id,name,date,latitude,longitude,description from events where date >= \$1::timestamptz and date <= \$2::timestamptz order by date desc limit \$3',
    [pad(from)+'-01-01T00:00:00Z', pad(to)+'-12-31T23:59:59Z', perWindow])))
const byId=new Map()
for(const b of batches) for(const r of b) byId.set(r.id,r)
const all=[...byId.values()].sort((a,b)=>new Date(a.date)-new Date(b.date)).slice(0,limit)
console.log('TOTAL fetched:', all.length)
console.log('geolocated  :', all.filter(r=>r.latitude!=null&&r.longitude!=null).length)
console.log('documented  :', all.filter(r=>(r.description||'').trim()).length)
console.log('earliest    :', all[0].name.replace(/\s+/g,' '), '|', all[0].date.toISOString().slice(0,10))
console.log('latest      :', all.at(-1).name.replace(/\s+/g,' '), '|', all.at(-1).date.toISOString().slice(0,10))
"
```
